title: sub-V182o_ses-260724 probeC (32-ch V-probe) was silently mislabeled V3d/V3a via a generic dual-area convention meant for 128-ch probes; corrected to a single area V3v by explicit user confirmation.
note: Surfaced while auditing the freshly-rebuilt 22-session TFR corpus (fig05-p0-dB-averaging-fix-20260811.json) for completeness -- session 260724 was missing 3 of its 5 sidecar-listed areas (V3, V3a, V3d never made it into the TFR corpus at all). Investigating the gap surfaced a real mislabeling bug, not just a missing-run gap.

claims.statement: D:/nwb/omission/sub-V182o_ses-260724.nwb's general/extracellular_ephys/electrodes/location field is bare 'V3' for all 32 channels of probe_2_lfp (probeC) -- not 'V3a'/'V3d'. The other two probes on this session are the standard 128-channel type (128x PFC, 128x FEF).

jnwb/sequence_layout.py's parse_probe_areas() treats bare 'V3' as the dual pair (V3d, V3a) by convention -- correct for this corpus's standard 128-channel V3 probes, where V3d occupies ch 0-64 and V3a occupies ch 64-128. scripts/archive_oneoff/build_session_sidecars.py's channel_slice_for_area() calls (both the per-electrode assignment loop and the probe_meta/channel_slices builder) never passed the probe's actual channel count, defaulting to PROBE_N_CHANNELS=128. For this one 32-channel probe, the boundary check 'ch.start <= local < ch.stop' against a 128-channel-based V3d slice (0-64) is true for every real channel (local 0-31), so every channel was assigned V3d and V3a was never reached -- confirmed on disk in the pre-fix D:/analysis/metadata/sub-V182o_ses-260724/electrodes.csv: 32/32 probeC rows labeled V3d, zero V3a. build_channel_area_vector.py's own consistency check (declared n_channels vs area-slice span) correctly caught the resulting contradiction (n_channels=32 vs slice span 128) and excluded the probe from channel_area_vector.csv rather than propagate it -- that guard worked as designed; the bug was entirely upstream in the sidecar generator.
claims.receipt: Pre-fix D:/analysis/metadata/sub-V182o_ses-260724/electrodes.csv: probeC 32/32 rows area='V3d', 0 rows 'V3a'. Pre-fix probe_areas.json probeC: n_channels=32, channel_slices={'V3d':{0,64},'V3a':{64,128}} -- internally contradictory (slice span 128 != declared n_channels 32).

claims.statement: User (Hamm) confirmed by hand: this 32-channel probe is anatomically a single region, V3v (ventral V3), not a dorsal/anterior V3d/V3a split -- it is the one exceptional probe in the corpus of this type. For area-level statistical pooling, V3v should be grouped with plain 'V3' (the label the C31o sessions' own unsplit V3 probes carry), not with the V3a/V3d pooling convention documented in jnwb-tfr/SKILL.md ('V3a and V3d are the upper/lower halves of one probe shank ... pool to V3a/d for inference').
claims.receipt: Direct user instruction, this session, 2026-08-12: '260724's probe C should be 32 channels; a vprobe; that is the exceptional session; so check it' followed by 'just remember that this 32 channel is all V3v; edit its nwb or tables; only this one probe is V3v but we group it with V3s'.

claims.statement: Fixed at the derived-table layer, not by editing the raw NWB (primary source data, left untouched). (1) Added SINGLE_AREA_OVERRIDES = {('sub-V182o_ses-260724','probeC'): 'V3v'} to build_session_sidecars.py, consulted before the generic parse_probe_areas() dual-split rule. (2) Fixed the general n_channels bug alongside it: both channel_slice_for_area() call sites now receive the probe's real observed channel count instead of a hardcoded 128 -- inert for every other probe in the corpus (all standard 128-ch), but the fix that would have prevented this bug for any future non-standard probe. (3) Regenerated this session's sidecar: probeC now resolves to areas=['V3v'], channel_slices={'V3v':{0,32}}, n_channels=32; electrodes.csv shows 32/32 rows area='V3v'. (4) build_channel_area_vector.py separately needed its own fix to run at all post-corpus-rebuild -- tfr_corpus_index() only globbed *.npy, but the whole 22-session corpus is now *.npz (precompute_tfr_arrays_v2.py's format); fixed to glob both, matching the same accommodation already made in compute_channel_band_power_census_v2.py. Also fixed a WindowsPath-not-JSON-serializable receipt-write bug (same bug class as the one already fixed in the fig05 census script) found while re-running it. Rebuilt channel_area_vector.csv: probeC/V3v now resolves correctly (32 channels, 22/22 sessions, 0 unresolved area tokens). (5) Backfilling the missing V3v TFR arrays via scripts/run_tfr_precompute_batch.sh sub-V182o_ses-260724 (also re-writes the already-correct FEF/PFC files identically -- idempotent).
claims.receipt: git diff scripts/archive_oneoff/build_session_sidecars.py, scripts/build_channel_area_vector.py, this session. Post-fix probe_areas.json probeC: {'location_raw':'V3','areas':['V3v'],'channel_slices':{'V3v':{'start':0,'stop':32}},'n_channels':32}. Post-fix electrodes.csv: 32/32 probeC rows area='V3v'. channel_area_vector.csv post-rebuild: probe_letter=C area=V3v count=32 for sub-V182o_ses-260724; 8,992 channels total, 22 sessions, 0 unresolved area tokens.

issues: The V3v-groups-with-plain-V3 pooling convention (not V3a/V3d) is documented here but NOT YET wired into any downstream consumer script (GLMM area-pooling logic appears in ~38 files per a corpus grep, none touched this session). Apply it when Fig05/Fig06's GLMM scripts are actually built/rerun against this corpus -- flagging now so it isn't missed, deliberately not touching 38 files pre-emptively before those figures are even started.

This was found by manually auditing one session's area list against its sidecar during a routine corpus-completeness check -- worth asking whether any OTHER non-standard-channel-count probes exist elsewhere in the corpus that haven't been individually audited the same way. Not systematically checked beyond this one session.
falsifier: Superseded once the V3v TFR backfill completes and channel counts/areas for sub-V182o_ses-260724 are re-verified end to end (sidecar -> channel_area_vector -> TFR files all agreeing on V3v/32ch), and once the V3v-with-plain-V3 pooling convention is actually applied in whichever GLMM script consumes area-pooled TFR data for Fig05/Fig06.
